findings.fix: correct: **Strict participant control.** [keep both quotations] A manager attends the retro only if the entire Scrum Team invites them; once there, they support and do not steer. (Re-anchor as participant-set-control.)

The distillation's own Concept 2 says both rules 'create a safe container'.

notes: Deep ref and converted source read in full; all quotations checked against the source. This file shares the AAR distillation's two imports and extends them: the invented owner-and-date read-back at the retro close (Relevance, Concept 13, Phase 5 question, a What-to-Look-For row, When-to-Use, the worked example's attribution line, and an anti-pattern) and the manager-speaks-last concept (Concept 10, Phase 0 question, What-to-Look-For row, an anti-pattern). It adds a named-owner requirement for decisions and actions (Concept 7) that the source does not state, and 'one-constraint' narrowing of the source's 'one or two'. The Named-limits paragraph is wrong in two places: the source does address psychological-safety conditions and facilitation craft, and it does touch remote and Kanban retros. The worked-example scenario itself (√12 → 3 votes, surprise check, DoD change) is sound hypothetical application; only its closing attribution line overclaims. TC 25-20 ('Train to weakness, not to strength'; closing comments), OPL (Retrospectives; Design of Experiments) and OB (conformity, groupthink, attribution bias) integration rows check out.
